regime: Inflation re-accelerating into firm nominal demand; labour steady, conditions still loose
executive_summary: Week 42 was an inflation week. September CPI ran hot on core, 0.34% m/m against 0.22% consensus, with core y/y at 2.56% and headline at 3.74%. PPI was hotter still: headline +1.3% m/m and core +0.7% m/m, 5.0% y/y. Euro area HICP rose to 3.75% y/y, above the 3.6% expectation. Three inflation prints in two regions point the same way, which is signal, not noise. Activity did not soften to offset it: retail sales rose 0.77% m/m and industrial production 0.66% m/m. Labour stayed low-hire, low-fire, with initial claims at 199,000. Financial conditions remain loose, NFCI at -0.499, though it has tightened slightly two weeks running. The 10y yield fell 18bp to 5.10% over 5 days despite the hot prints, while the 2y was flat at 4.77%. The mix argues against near-term easing. Sentiment has no logged stance and its latest print is from August.

narrative.title: Inflation and policy
narrative.body: The ISM to PPI to CPI chain is lining up. September PPI headline rose 1.3% m/m, about 0.7pp above consensus (unconfirmed), and y/y reached 6.3%. Energy drove much of that, but core PPI also jumped to +0.7% m/m and 5.0% y/y. CPI followed in the same month: core +0.34% m/m against 0.22% expected, core y/y 2.56% against 2.4%, headline y/y 3.74% against 3.6%. Since PPI leads CPI by 1 to 3 months, the October and November CPI prints carry upside risk. The latest core PCE in the log is August at 3.0% y/y, so the Fed's preferred gauge has not yet absorbed September. The FOMC upper bound sits at 4.0% after the September decision. In Europe, HICP rose to 3.75% y/y from 3.23%, a 3-year high led by energy, with core steady near 2.5%. Two regions with energy-led headline acceleration and firmer core in the US is the alignment to watch. Market-implied inflation is calm: 5y5y breakevens held at 2.33% and 10y breakevens at 2.35%, both unchanged on the week.

narrative.title: Labour
narrative.body: Labour is not turning. Initial claims were 199,000 against 200,000 consensus (unconfirmed), the 4-week average 198,500, and continuing claims flat at 1.71M. The other legs of the chain are older baseline prints: JOLTS openings fell 256k to 7.08M in August, quits rate 1.9%, ADP added 90k in September and NFP added 29k with unemployment up 0.1pt to 4.2%. Average hourly earnings rose 0.13% m/m and 3.0% y/y, so wages are not feeding the CPI acceleration. The pattern is slow hiring without layoffs. A turn would need claims rising alongside weaker openings and payrolls; only the claims leg updated this week and it was flat. The view changes if the 4-week average climbs above 215,000 or continuing claims pass 1.8M.

narrative.title: Growth, housing and sentiment
narrative.body: Nominal demand is firm. Retail sales rose 0.77% m/m against 0.3% consensus after +1.29% in August, and 6.29% y/y. Gas stations contributed much of the beat on price, so real consumption is softer than the headline, and ex-gas was reported near +0.2% (unconfirmed). Ex-auto sales rose 0.72%. Industrial production added 0.66% m/m, 2.25% y/y, with capacity utilisation up to 76.85%. Both are hard-data support for Q3 GDP after Q2 at 2.2% SAAR. August core capex orders rose 1.56%. Housing is weak at a low level: existing home sales rose 1.5% to 3.99M SAAR, slightly above the 3.95M consensus, but this is a lagging closings count. The leading series, permits, fell 2.1% to 1.40M in August, and starts fell 2.6%. Sentiment has no stance; the latest UMich reading is August at 51.7, down 3.5 points, which is stale for this synthesis.

narrative.title: Financial conditions
narrative.body: Conditions are loose but drifting tighter at the margin. NFCI rose 0.008 to -0.499, a second small tightening week, still well below zero. HY OAS widened 8bp to 3.23% and IG OAS 2bp to 0.84%, both from tight levels. The curve flattened: 10y-2y narrowed 12bp to 0.35% and 10y-3m 16bp to 0.83%, as the 10y fell 18bp to 5.10% and the 2y held at 4.77%. The 10y real yield fell 14bp to 2.78%, so the long-end rally was real rates, not breakevens. VIX rose 1.1 points to 16.46. Long yields falling into hot inflation prints is a mismatch with the macro data; if it reflects growth worries, it should show up in wider spreads and weaker activity data first. Q3 SLOOS showed net C&I tightening at 0%, so bank credit is not a constraint.

regime_watch: The firming-inflation regime is confirmed if core CPI m/m stays above 0.3% next month, core PCE for September rises from 3.0% y/y, and core PPI does not retrace. It is denied if energy reverses and core PPI drops back near 0.3% m/m. A shift toward slowdown would need claims above a 215,000 4-week average, falling permits again, and HY spreads widening well beyond this week's 8bp, together rather than alone.
